answer: A farm therefore spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the summit quota and the vertex admission check. Because the pulse audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. Admission is capped at 6 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. That is 34 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
